title: Add an ID3v2 dissector and ability to dissect UTF-16 strings with BOM.
description:
Call the ID3v2 dissector from the mpeg-audio dissector.

Fixes #17991.

notes.body: Oh yeah, one note: I contemplated putting UTF_16_BOM next to UTF_16 but I spent so much of my career telling people not to reorder enums that I didn't.  But in this case it doesn't really matter; I could go either way.

Hi Jeff 

May be split the change on 2 MR ? (one for ENC_UTF_16_BOM) ? and an other for ID3v2 dissector ?

can you fix also

```
packet-id3v2.c:400:1: warning: no previous prototype for function 'dissect_id3v2' [-Wmissing-prototypes]
packet-id3v2.c:399:1: note: declare 'static' if the function is not intended to be used outside of this translation unit
```

added 6 commits
  • b0895c38...109b92b5 - 4 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 07e653b5 - Add ENC_UTF_16_BOM in which we read the BOM to determine the byte order.
  • 216ef979 - Add an ID3v2 dissector.
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6412/diffs?diff_id=350987751&start_sha=b0895c380bef383e176d103984ada84b3f3cf792)

I fixed the warning, thanks.

I could do 2 PRs but I can't find a way to implement dependencies between them - that's why I did 2 commits instead.  (Gitlab supports merge request dependencies but says it's a PREMIUM - their, er, wording - feature.)

Actually, I'm thinking I should rework the UTF-16-with-BOM patch to just use the existing UTF-16 encoding value and then, if we have 2+ bytes, check if they are the BOM and if so ignore the encoding (big/little endian) that the caller gave (instead using the value determined from the BOM).  That's probably more inline with a real UTF-16 implementation after all...  @guyharris what do you think?

Are you interested in picking this back up? I think that the approach mentioned in the last comment makes sense.

I do think that you could split it into two MRs; just do the encoding first. It has separate utility. (IIRC, I think the XML dissector, maybe others, could use it.)
See !10954 for updating this to the current mpeg-audio dissector.
